goal: Create scripts/chain/gates.mjs — the Option C kernel. One CLI call collapses spec-lint, validation, scope compliance, claim-checking and verdict consistency into a single tool call, emitting one JSON GateReport on stdout and human lines on stderr. gates.mjs itself stays PURE: every check is a function over already-collected inputs, and all impurity (git, spawn, disk) arrives through an injected io capability object defaulting to evidence.mjs / spec-lint.mjs / return-lint.mjs. This never validates a return, never writes an envelope, never touches an OUTCOMES value, and never rolls anything back — it reports, the caller decides.
constraints: conventions.md 2026-08-01 'every functional commit bumps the version field in .claude-plugin/plugin.json and the commit message ends with ; bump 0.<major>.<minor>' — read the CURRENT value from the file (0.1.74 as of #25's ship — re-verify) and increment the patch by exactly one; do not assume a value. This is the single bump for the whole #28 PR.

backend-notes.md 2026-08-05 'process.exit(main(...)) truncates large stdout when stdout is a pipe — use process.exitCode = main(...)'. A GateReport with many violations can exceed 64KB and this CLI's whole purpose is to be spawned by a consumer, so its stdout IS a pipe in the normal case. Mirror spec-lint.mjs:522-531 exactly.

backend-notes.md 2026-08-05 'a CLI-as-library refactor needs its usage/parse-error path to throw a tagged error class rather than call process.exit from a helper' — use a local UsageError; main(argv) -> number always RETURNS its exit code.
backend-notes.md 2026-08-05 'a hand-rolled for...of over a spec field crashes or misbehaves if the field is a string' — guard every spec array field with Array.isArray before iterating.

conventions.md 2026-08-01 'Prefer structural impossibility to a test assertion, and a whitelist to a blacklist. Where a constraint must be enumerated, enumerate what is ALLOWED' — CHECK_NAMES and PROTECTED_PREFIXES are frozen closed allow-lists.

conventions.md 2026-08-01 'Filters apply to what an agent reads, never to what a check verifies' — scope_compliance always sees the UNFILTERED touched list; no noise-glob filtering is ever applied to it.
backend-notes.md 2026-08-01 'Violation shape' + the exactly-one-violation deepEqual convention — every single-mutation negative asserts the full check object, never just truthiness.
Chain -> cmux is the permitted import direction; never the reverse.
Zero dependencies: node builtins plus this repo's own modules only.
acceptance_criteria: CLI surface, both subcommands, each pinned by a real-subprocess test (spawnSync of `node scripts/chain/gates.mjs ...`, not just an in-process main() call): `node scripts/chain/gates.mjs baseline --task <slug> --slice <slice_id> [--reason <text>]` and `node scripts/chain/gates.mjs check --task <slug> --slice <slice_id> [--checks a,b,c]`. Common options --checkout / --repo / --root mirror dispatch.mjs's (dispatch.mjs:21-22). An unknown subcommand, an unknown --checks name, or a missing required flag is a UsageError -> exit 2, naming the offending token; --checks NEVER silently ignores an unknown name.

FAIL-CLOSED BASELINE ORDERING (the single most important behavior in this file): `baseline` captures once and REFUSES (exit 2, EvidenceError 'baseline_exists') rather than overwrite an existing baseline for that slice — an overwrite at gate time is exactly what a bypass looks like. `check` NEVER lazily captures: when no baseline exists for the slice, the two baseline-dependent checks (diff_matches_claims, scope_compliance) each return { ok: false, hard_fail: true } with a note naming the expected baseline path and the remediation. Asserted directly, plus a named degenerate 'check captures the baseline lazily when absent' which must fail the suite (a baseline captured after the work produces an empty touched set — a silent pass on an out-of-scope or protected-path edit).

Baseline path is <stateDir>/chain/baseline.<slice_id>.json, derived via taskPaths() from scripts/cmux/resolve.mjs so teardown's existing wholesale stateDir sweep collects it with no teardown change. Asserted.

GateReport is emitted as exactly ONE line of JSON on stdout and nothing else; every human line goes to stderr (mirrors dispatch.mjs:24-26 and spec-lint.mjs --json). A test asserts stdout parses as a single JSON object even when checks produce many violations. hard_fail === checks.some(c => c.hard_fail === true) and violations === checks.filter(c => c.ok === false).map(c => ({item, hard_fail, note})) — both derivations pinned.
Exit codes: 0 when violations is empty; 1 when violations is non-empty (hard or not — the caller reads hard_fail from the JSON); 2 for usage/operational error. Pinned by real-subprocess tests.

EVERY check returns EVIDENCE on pass, not just a reason on fail — asserted per check, for all eight. A passing artifacts_exist note reads like 'exists, 2.1KB'; a passing scope_compliance note names the touched count and the paths; a passing verdict_consistent note names the verdict and finding count. A named degenerate 'note is empty string on pass' fails the suite for every check.

artifacts_exist / files_non_empty / json_parses each return one { item, ok, hard_fail: false, note } per resolved artifact set. The artifact set is [specPathFor(paths, sliceId)] plus every returns/<sliceId>.<attempt>.{json,md} present in paths.returnsDir; zero return files makes artifacts_exist ok:false. json_parses covers .json artifacts only and its note explicitly states that .md returns are excluded and why (they are not JSON) — not silently skipped.

diff_matches_claims: every path claimed in a return envelope's body.changes[] (leading token of each '<path> - <summary>' entry, normalized POSIX, leading './' stripped) must appear in the touched set. Unmatched -> { ok: false, hard_fail: false } naming EVERY unmatched path, never just the first. A markdown-kind return with no structured changes yields ok:true with a note saying explicitly that no structured changes were claimed — never a silent pass with an empty note.

scope_compliance, the protected-path half: PROTECTED_PREFIXES is a frozen, exactly-two-entry, glob-free list ['.claude/dev-team/memory/', '.claude/dev-team/config.md']. A touched path P is protected iff P === '.claude/dev-team/config.md' OR P.startsWith('.claude/dev-team/memory/'). Any protected touch is { ok: false, hard_fail: true } and the note NAMES EVERY offending path. Drift guard asserts BOTH deepEqual on the array AND Object.isFrozen (conventions.md 2026-08-08). This is ADR-016's first mechanical backstop for the memory single-writer rule.

scope_compliance, the ordinary half: a touched path outside spec.files_in_scope but not protected is a CORRECTABLE WARNING — { ok: false, hard_fail: false } — never hard_fail. Both halves present in one run produce ONE check with ok:false, hard_fail:true, and a note listing the two sets separately.

scope_compliance named degenerates, each asserted and each failing the suite: 'always ok:true'; 'a diff-only comparison blind to reversions and untracked files'; 'first-offender-only naming'; 'a protected path listed in files_in_scope treated as exempt' (listing a protected path in files_in_scope must NOT exempt it — asserted directly as a positive requirement too).

scope_compliance is additionally asserted end-to-end against real git fixtures (reusing test/cmux-dispatch.test.mjs:101's makeGitCheckout idiom, never a mocked collector) for: a rename entry; an untracked file inside a brand-new directory; a baseline-dirty file restored to its original bytes (must count as touched); a baseline-dirty file left as the user's own untouched edit (must NOT count as touched); and a newly-untracked file under a protected prefix (must hard_fail).

spec_lint calls lintSpec(spec, root) from scripts/spec-lint.mjs — NEVER main(), which writes to stdout and would corrupt the single-JSON-line contract. ok === result.ok; the note carries the failure and warning counts plus each failure rendered '<check>: <detail>'. hard_fail: false (a spec-lint failure is correctable). A source-text test pins that 'main' is not imported from spec-lint.mjs.

tests_pass is a check FACTORY: spec.validation_commands maps to ONE NAMED check per command, item id `tests_pass(<cmd>)`, never one merged check. EVERY command runs; a failure in one never short-circuits another. Asserted with three commands where the first and third fail: three checks present, all three notes populated, exactly two ok:false. A named degenerate 'all validation_commands merged into a single tests_pass check' fails the suite.

A failing validation command is { ok: false, hard_fail: false } — evidence for the repair loop, never a runner error. Timeout, missing-binary and refused are classified as DISTINCT outcomes in the note (drawn from the injected RunResult's `classified` field, never re-derived here). Truncated or absent output on an abnormal exit is reported as evidence, never as 'no failures'.

verdict_consistent is CONSISTENCY-REFUTATION ONLY. One INDEPENDENT check per reviewer envelope with distinguishable item ids (`verdict_consistent(<stem>)`). Variant A: verdict 'pass' with any finding of severity 'critical' -> { ok: false, hard_fail: true }, present in violations[], note naming EVERY critical finding (file/line/summary). Variant B: verdict 'changes-needed' with zero findings -> { ok: true, hard_fail: false, note: 'changes-needed with 0 findings - blocking reasoning may be in Must-fix prose' }, explicitly ABSENT from violations[] (asserted by name). Both variants independently asserted.

verdict_consistent additionally: a genuinely self-consistent verdict produces zero violations for all three enum values including 'inconclusive'; an N-panel input produces N independent checks and never one merged verdict (asserted with N=3, checking the item ids are distinct and the count is 3); and an end-to-end test against a real markdown body containing BOTH an illustrative fenced example and the real Verdict block asserts the REAL one is read.

verdict_consistent named degenerates, each failing the suite: 'always ok:true'; 'ok = verdict !== \'pass\''; 'ok = !findings.some(critical)' — the verdict-BLIND variant a naive read of references/qa-gate.md's 'critical findings block' rule would produce, since that sentence says nothing about the verdict field.

DESIGN INVARIANTS, each with its own assertion: (a) gates.mjs never calls ladder.validateReturn and never imports return-envelope.schema.json — those remain the only validator over returns/, and this checks AFTER a dispatch is already confirmed `completed` by that authority (source-text test pins both absences); (b) gates.mjs never writes any file under returns/ and never writes an envelope (a test runs a full check against a fixture tree and asserts the returns/ directory mtimes and contents are unchanged); (c) gates.mjs never reads, writes or references an OUTCOMES value (source-text test); (d) verdict_consistent never rewrites a worker-authored verdict field (a test asserts the return file on disk is byte-identical after the check) and never aggregates a panel; (e) no auto-rollback, revert, reset or delete of anything a check finds (source-text test over a forbidden-verb list, needle built from fragments per conventions.md 2026-08-08).

PURITY: every check function is exported and pure over its inputs; all impurity arrives via an injected io object (io.touchedPaths, io.runValidationCommand, io.lintSpec, io.readArtifact, io.extractVerdictBlock) that defaults to the real wiring. The check-logic tests pass CANNED results with no real spawning — asserted by a test that runs the full check suite with a fully-mocked io and confirms zero child processes and zero git calls (e.g. by pointing cwd at a non-repo tmpdir and asserting no throw).

No new .schema.json file is added (verified by the reviewer). If one were ever added it must go in test/schema.test.mjs:64's BUDGETED_SCHEMAS list — the BUDGET-walk list — NOT the inline conditional-keyword array at test/schema.test.mjs:29, which is a different check.

Review depth: code-reviewer-deep is REQUIRED, and this file is the primary subject of issue #28's adversarial 3-reviewer panel + dev-team:test-engineer mutation pass (mutation pass runs FIRST and ALONE on the frozen tree, per the qa-lead consult). Security-control surfaces to lens: the protected-path hard_fail (a security control), agent-controlled command execution via tests_pass, and the fail-closed baseline ordering.
`node --test test/chain-gates.test.mjs` green; total #28 suite growth <= 10s across all three specs; no cmux, no claude, no model, no network, no GUI.

PATTERN TO MIRROR — the exitCode-not-exit CLI tail, scripts/spec-lint.mjs:522-531:

    const invokedDirectly = process.argv[1] && realpathOr(process.argv[1]) === realpathOr(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))
    if (invokedDirectly) {
      // process.exitCode, not process.exit: stdout is a pipe when a consumer
      // spawns this CLI ... pipe writes are asynchronous - process.exit() tears
      // the process down before Node flushes the buffer, silently truncating a
      // large --json payload.
      process.exitCode = main(process.argv.slice(2))
    }

realpathOr must realpath BOTH sides — the ESM loader realpaths import.meta.url while argv[1] stays literal, so under a symlinked path component (macOS TMPDIR is /var -> /private/var) a literal compare is silently false and the CLI no-ops. This is a multi-site pattern already (return-lint.mjs:523, adapter-claude.mjs, spec-lint.mjs) — copy the existing shape and add a symlinked-invocation regression test (backend-notes.md 2026-08-02).

PATTERN TO MIRROR — main() returning an exit code with a tagged usage error, scripts/spec-lint.mjs:497-520: a try/catch around the whole body mapping UsageError to 2 and anything else to 2 as well, writing err.message (UsageError) or err.stack (anything else) to stderr.

DO NOT UNIFY WITH contract.mjs:39's PROTECTED_PATH_COMPONENTS (= ['.claude', '.git', '.vscode', '.idea', '.husky', '.devcontainer']). That constant answers a DIFFERENT question (where a dispatcher may site an agent-writable directory) at a DIFFERENT time (path derivation, resolve.mjs:51-62's assertSafePath). This slice's set answers 'did a coder touch the memory single-writer surface'. Two entries, exact-prefix, glob-free, deliberately narrow — scripts/** and hooks/** are this repo's own PRODUCT and are NOT protected. Put a comment at the PROTECTED_PREFIXES definition site stating the non-unification and why, so a future reader reads it as a decision rather than an omission. Anything that would need general glob logic can only ever produce a correctable warning, never a hard_fail — that is what keeps hard_fail auditable by eye.

WHY THE PROTECTED SET IS ONLY TWO ENTRIES, AND WHY hard_fail IS ONLY HERE: this is the one check in the whole initiative with hard_fail:true, and its entire job is catching what a bypass would look like. A two-entry exact-prefix list can be verified correct by reading it. A glob engine cannot.
